{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Home Assistant Nightly Beta Tests

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 0 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:      
  beta-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Install pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: 'pnpm'
      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install
      - name: E2E Tests
        run: TAG=beta pnpm test:ci
      - name: Create coverage
        run: pnpm coverage:report
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: test-report
          path: |
            playwright-report/
            coverage/
          retention-days: 30",
  "rationale": "The job has representative successful-duration history (five recent scheduled runs, all successful, each about 10-12 minutes). Adding an explicit job timeout bounds runaway consumption per P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT while preserving every existing step, trigger, and artifact upload. The 30-minute limit gives roughly 3x operational headroom above observed durations, mitigating the contraindication that valid slow runs could exceed the limit. No permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations, or new network access are added.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
